options: A study of cognitive processes & behavior
questions.explanation: Psychology is the scientific study of mind (cognitive processes) and behavior. It is more than an art of living or a thought process, which describe only parts of it.

questions.q: A broad field of study that explores a variety of questions about thoughts, feelings and actions is ____?
questions.explanation: Psychology specifically investigates thoughts, feelings and actions of individuals. Social science is a broader umbrella that also covers economics, sociology and politics, so it is less precise.

questions.q: A systematic assessment that provides information on political views, consumer buying habits and many other topics is called ____?
questions.explanation: A survey systematically collects self-reported information from many people, which is how opinions on politics or buying habits are gathered. Experiments manipulate variables, and standardized or psychological tests measure abilities or traits.
Psychology comes from the Greek words psyche (mind or soul) and logos (study). Hence psychology originally meant the study of the mind or soul.

questions.q: Who established psychology laboratory in Germany?
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Wundt set up the first experimental psychology laboratory at Leipzig, Germany, in 1879. Skinner and Thorndike worked in the USA, and Freud developed psychoanalysis in Vienna rather than a lab.

questions.q: To help people to function effectively and fulfill their own unique potential" is the aim of ____
questions.explanation: Humanistic psychology (Maslow, Rogers) emphasizes personal growth, free will and self-actualization, i.e., helping people fulfill their unique potential.

questions.q: Behaviorists use a learning process to change abnormal behavior is called ____?
questions.explanation: Behaviorists treat abnormal behavior as learned, so they use conditioning (classical and operant techniques such as desensitization or reinforcement) to change it. Gestalt and rationalism are not behaviorist learning processes.

questions.q: The study of changes in behavior during life time is called
questions.explanation: Developmental psychology studies how behavior, cognition and emotion change across the lifespan, from infancy through old age. Maturation is only one factor within that study.

questions.q: The study of differences and similarities in the behavior of animals of different species is called
questions.explanation: Comparative psychology compares behavior across species to understand evolutionary and functional similarities and differences. Cultural psychology compares human cultures, not species.
